page: Amazon Web Services c8id.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor comprising 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The CPU subsystem is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration extensions including Intel AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512. System memory totals 128.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, yielding a compute-standard ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Storage and networking subsystems are provisioned for low latency and high local throughput. The instance integrates 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store volume, eliminating external network storage overhead for temporary files, local scratch space, or working datasets. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps, managed directly by Nitro offload cards.

Benchmark results show strong to top-tier execution across multi-threaded computational workloads. The system attained a Geekbench multi-core score of 21428.0, alongside Clang software compilation throughput scored at 59025.0 and ray tracing at 91339.0, placing it within the top 10 percent of tested servers. Memory performance reaches 196.82 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads, and Redis operations achieved 112.86 million SET operations per second. Static web serving throughput reached 109.49 GB/sec.

Because the system allocates 2.0 GB of memory per core, it offers high compute density per gigabyte of RAM, though it is not configured for large in-memory datasets. The combination of hardware-accelerated matrix instructions, high clock speeds, and bundled local NVMe storage provides strong resource efficiency for continuous integration pipelines, software build farms, video transcoding, static web serving, and database workloads requiring fast local scratch access.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.16xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro-based cloud instance powered by a 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz with a 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a bundled 3800 GB local NVMe SSD and a 30 Gbps baseline network interface. The processor features dedicated hardware vector acceleration, including AMX and AVX-512 extensions. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution, achieving 21,428.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 59,025.0 in Clang software compilation, and 109.49 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Redis performance scales to 112.86 million operations per second. While the 2 GB per core allocation limits large in-memory footprints, the combination of dense compute, integrated high-speed NVMe storage, and high networking throughput provides strong resource efficiency for CI/CD compilation, distributed caching, media encoding, and database operations.
